templates.pattern:
Statement: 'Providing high-speed internet access to all villages is as important as building roads and schools for national development.'
Assumption I: Internet access is a key driver of development.
Assumption II: Currently, villages lack high-speed internet.
Assumption III: Roads and schools are accepted as essential for development.
Assumption IV: Internet access is more important than other basic needs.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: Internet as a development driver (I) is the premise — implicit. Villages lacking it (II) motivates the call for provision — implicit. Roads/schools being accepted as essential (III) is implicit — that's why it's used as a comparison. IV (internet > other needs) contradicts 'as important as' — not assumed. I, II and III are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'The increasing use of private vehicles in cities is leading to pollution and congestion. Citizens must be encouraged to use public transport.'
Assumption I: Public transport reduces pollution and congestion.
Assumption II: Citizens currently prefer private vehicles.
Assumption III: Public transport infrastructure is adequate.
Assumption IV: Encouraging citizens will change their behaviour.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: Public transport reducing pollution (I) is why it's recommended — implicit. Citizens preferring private vehicles (II) is the behaviour to be changed — implicit. Adequate infrastructure (III) is not assumed — the call to encourage may precede improvement. Encouragement changing behaviour (IV) is assumed for the suggestion to make sense — implicit. I, II and IV are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'The UPSC should revise its examination pattern to test analytical abilities rather than just factual recall.'
Assumption I: The current UPSC pattern tests mostly factual recall.
Assumption II: Analytical ability is more important for a civil servant than factual knowledge.
Assumption III: A revised pattern will accurately measure analytical ability.
Assumption IV: Civil servants currently lack analytical skills.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: Current pattern testing recall (I) is the premise for revision — implicit. Analytical ability being more relevant (II) is the rationale — implicit. Revised pattern measuring it accurately (III) is assumed for the revision to be useful — implicit. IV (current servants lacking skills) is not assumed. I, II and III are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'Despite having a robust legal framework, gender-based violence in India remains alarmingly high. Awareness campaigns and community education are more urgently needed.'
Assumption I: Legal frameworks alone cannot eliminate gender-based violence.
Assumption II: Awareness campaigns reduce gender-based violence.
Assumption III: The legal framework in India is adequate.
Assumption IV: Community education changes attitudes towards gender.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: Laws being insufficient (I) is directly implied — implicit. Awareness reducing violence (II) is why campaigns are recommended — implicit. III (laws being adequate) is explicitly stated — not an assumption. Community education changing attitudes (IV) is the mechanism behind the recommendation — implicit. I, II and IV are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'The state government's decision to waive farm loans will provide relief to distressed farmers but may create a moral hazard for future borrowers.'
Assumption I: Farmers are in financial distress.
Assumption II: Loan waiver helps farmers in the short term.
Assumption III: Future borrowers may default expecting waivers.
Assumption IV: Loan waivers are the best solution for farmer distress.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: Farmers being distressed (I) motivates the waiver — implicit. Short-term relief (II) is what the waiver provides — implicit. Moral hazard for future borrowers (III) is the risk being flagged — implicit. IV (best solution) contradicts the moral hazard concern — not assumed. I, II and III are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'Implementing a uniform education curriculum across the country will help bridge the quality gap between rural and urban schools.'
Assumption I: There is a quality gap between rural and urban schools.
Assumption II: A uniform curriculum will reduce the quality gap.
Assumption III: Rural schools lack qualified teachers to implement the curriculum.
Assumption IV: Curriculum is a major factor determining education quality.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: Quality gap (I) is the problem being addressed — implicit. Uniform curriculum bridging the gap (II) is the logic — implicit. Teacher quality (III) is a concern but not assumed here — it's a counter-argument. Curriculum affecting quality (IV) is the basis of the policy — implicit. I, II and IV are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'The finance minister urged banks to reduce interest rates on home loans to boost the sluggish real estate sector.'
Assumption I: High interest rates are discouraging home buyers.
Assumption II: Banks can reduce interest rates if they choose to.
Assumption III: Real estate sector growth contributes to economic growth.
Assumption IV: The finance minister has authority over bank interest rates.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: High rates discouraging buyers (I) is why reduction is urged — implicit. Banks having the ability (II) is assumed in the urging — implicit. Real estate boosting economy (III) is why the sector's sluggishness matters — implicit. IV (authority) — the minister urged, not ordered — so no authority is assumed. I, II and III are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'The increasing prevalence of lifestyle diseases like diabetes and hypertension underscores the need for preventive healthcare rather than curative treatment.'
Assumption I: Lifestyle diseases are largely preventable.
Assumption II: Preventive healthcare is more cost-effective than curative treatment.
Assumption III: Current healthcare system focuses more on curative treatment.
Assumption IV: Changing lifestyle can reduce incidence of these diseases.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: Preventability (I) is the basis for preventive focus — implicit. Cost-effectiveness (II) strengthens the case — implicit. Current curative focus (III) explains why a shift is needed — implicit. Lifestyle changes reducing incidence (IV) is the mechanism of prevention — implicit. All four are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'Bringing all citizens under the formal banking system is a prerequisite for effective implementation of Direct Benefit Transfer schemes.'
Assumption I: Currently, not all citizens have bank accounts.
Assumption II: DBT schemes require recipients to have bank accounts.
Assumption III: DBT is an effective way to deliver government benefits.
Assumption IV: Formal banking eliminates leakages in benefit transfers.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: Not all having accounts (I) is why inclusion is a prerequisite — implicit. DBT needing bank accounts (II) is the technical requirement — implicit. DBT being effective (III) is why the scheme is worth implementing — implicit. Formal banking eliminating leakages (IV) is the assumed benefit — implicit. All four are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'The WHO has warned that antibiotic resistance is one of the greatest threats to global health, food security and development.'
Assumption I: Antibiotic resistance is increasing globally.
Assumption II: WHO warnings are taken seriously by governments.
Assumption III: Antibiotic resistance affects food security.
Assumption IV: Human actions are contributing to antibiotic resistance.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: Resistance being a growing global problem (I) underlies the warning — implicit. WHO warnings being effective (II) is implicit — otherwise why warn? III is explicitly stated in the warning — not an assumption. Human contribution (IV) is implicit since it's a 'threat' being warned about — implied a preventable one. I, II and IV are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'The government should set up more cold storage facilities in rural areas to prevent post-harvest losses and improve farmers' income.'
Assumption I: Post-harvest losses are significant in rural areas.
Assumption II: Lack of cold storage is a major cause of post-harvest losses.
Assumption III: Improved storage will lead to better prices for farmers.
Assumption IV: Farmers currently have access to some cold storage facilities.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: Significant post-harvest losses (I) motivate the policy — implicit. Lack of storage causing losses (II) is why storage is the solution — implicit. Better storage leading to better income (III) is the assumed outcome — implicit. IV (some existing facilities) — 'more' implies some exist — implicit. All four are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'To address the alarming drop in groundwater levels in Punjab and Haryana, the government should incentivise farmers to shift to less water-intensive crops.'
Assumption I: Groundwater levels in Punjab and Haryana have dropped alarmingly.
Assumption II: Rice cultivation in these states consumes excessive groundwater.
Assumption III: Less water-intensive crops are economically viable for farmers.
Assumption IV: Farmers will respond to incentives by changing their crop pattern.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: I is explicitly stated — not fully an assumption, but forms the premise. II (current crops use excessive water) is why a shift is recommended — implicit. III (alternative crops being viable) is crucial for the incentive to work — implicit. IV (farmers responding to incentives) is assumed since incentives are proposed — implicit. II, III and IV are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'The recent rise in communal tensions in some parts of the country calls for immediate intervention by civil society and local administration to promote inter-community dialogue.'
Assumption I: Inter-community dialogue can reduce communal tensions.
Assumption II: Civil society and local administration have a role in maintaining communal harmony.
Assumption III: The central government alone cannot manage communal tensions.
Assumption IV: Communal tensions are caused by lack of dialogue between communities.
Which assumptions are implicit?
templates.explanation: Dialogue reducing tensions (I) is why it's recommended — implicit. Civil society's role (II) is the basis for 'calling' on them — implicit. III (central government unable alone) may be implied by calling on local/civil bodies, but is not directly assumed. IV (lack of dialogue causing tensions) is the assumed root cause — implicit. I, II and IV are implicit.
